concepts.def: Systematically examining an existing product to judge its strengths and weaknesses, often using criteria such as ACCESS FM.
An analysis checklist standing for Aesthetics, Cost, Customer, Environment, Size, Safety, Function and Materials.
Taking a product apart to study its internal components, materials, fixings and the methods used to manufacture and assemble it.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Learning From Existing Products — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Learning From Existing Products brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Learning From Existing Products.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In ACCESS FM, what does the first 'A' stand for?
options: Aesthetics
Assembly
Accuracy
Affordability

mcqs.q: Why might a designer disassemble an existing product?
options: To study its components, materials and assembly methods
To dispose of it in landfill
To make it lighter to post
To hide its brand name

mcqs.q: When learning from competitors' products, designers must avoid what?
options: Infringing patents and registered designs by copying
Looking at more than one product
Writing down their findings
Comparing prices

mcqs.q: What does an ergonomic evaluation of a product assess?
options: How comfortably and easily people can use it
How much profit it generates
How recyclable its packaging is
How quickly it can be advertised

mcqs.q: Is analysing existing products the same as copying them?
options: ACCESS FM is a British manufacturing safety standard.
No — analysis identifies strengths, weaknesses and gaps to inform your own original design; directly copying may infringe patents, trademarks or registered designs.
Product analysis is only legal on products more than 50 years old.
Designers are free to copy any product that is already on the market.

mcqs.q: What does ACCESS FM stand for?
options: ACCESS FM is a British manufacturing safety standard.
Aesthetics, Cost, Customer, Environment, Size, Safety, Function and Materials — a checklist of criteria for analysing a product.
Product analysis is only legal on products more than 50 years old.
ACCESS FM is a step-by-step method for assembling flat-pack products.

mcqs.q: Why disassemble a product during analysis rather than just look at it?
options: Disassembly reveals internal components, material choices, fixings and assembly methods that are invisible from outside, showing how the product was engineered and made.
Disassembly is only ever done to repair products that have broken.
Disassembly is legally required before any product can be resold.
ACCESS FM is a British manufacturing safety standard.
